citation.note: Wage Payment Law with Wage Theft Act (2019): N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.1 et seq. governs pay timing and requires written notice in advance of any wage, payday, or deduction change; Wage Theft Act extends statute of limitations to 6 years (6-year limitations period) with liquidated damages of 200% of wages due, plus attorney fees and costs.
Salary History Inquiry Block (§ 34:6B-20): Disable any form field attempting to request prior salary/wages from external candidates; log any such queries as compliance risk.

citation.note: Payroll and personnel record retention (N.J.S.A. 34:11D-6, 34:11-4.6): Payroll records retained 5 years; general employee records 3 years; personnel files 2 years after termination.
Earned Leave Accrual and Termination (§ 34:11D-1): Track accrued sick leave (1 hour per 30 hours worked, 40-hour max per year).

citation.note: WARN Act Trigger (§ 34:21-1 as amended): If planned layoff affects 100+ employees nationwide or 25+ employees in single event and employer has 100+ employees total, auto-flag and require 90-day notice scheduling; mandatory severance of 1 week per year of service plus 4 additional weeks if notice inadequate.

citation.note: Minimum wage $15.92/hour for employers with 6+ employees as of 2026, with annual CPI adjustments (N.J.S.A. 34:11-56a4).
Minimum wage $15.23/hour for employers with 5 or fewer employees as of 2026, with annual CPI adjustments (N.J.S.A. 34:11-56a4).
Minimum wage $14.20/hour for agricultural workers in 2026 (N.J.S.A. 34:11-56a4).

Diane B. Allen Equal Pay Act (N.J.S.A. 10:5-12): Unlawful to pay protected-class employees at lower rates for substantially similar work; 21 protected classes including race, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, marital status, genetic information.

Wage Theft Act Compliance (§ 34:11-4.1): Document all pay rate changes and provide written notice in advance; failure to provide notice triggers retaliation and wage-theft penalties (200% liquidated damages, attorney fees, 6-year statute of limitations).
Cannabis exception: N.J.S.A. 24:6I-52 protects lawful off-duty cannabis use and metabolites.

Data breach notification (N.J.S.A. 56:8-163): Notification to affected individuals in most expedient time possible without unreasonable delay; report to NJ Division of State Police before individual notifications.
